messages.author: 82933c06b1097cc4
messages.subject: singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts:
Hi, 
I am trying to do mqmscan with my RIL data, 7LGs, ~6,000 markers. According to the tutorial there are two approaches to fill in the missing data :1) mqmaugmentdata or 2) fill.geno. The first approach took super long (running on a cluster for >3 days and still not showing any results and is still running). The fill.geno only took a few seconds but when I proceed with the mqmscan, I got an error message and the calculation was stopped:

FATALError in mqmscan(AE, model = "dominance", pheno.col = "rep1") : 
 
 Singular matrix

Calls: mqmscan -> .C
Execution halted
Could anybody provide any suggestions as what should be done? My one way scan and two way scan was fine.
Thank you

messages.author: acb750e476c0ff5d
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts:
I'm having a similar error, the "singular matrix" error. I also had the "Some markers at the same position" error. I assume this is the map problem that Danny was talking about. I'm trying to follow his recommendation, but I'm using GigaMUGA data for my analysis. I started with 143,259 SNPs (the whole set) and dwindled it down to 31,642 SNPs that are informative between the two mouse strains of interest. Is this data set too big? I seem to have problem markers on every chromosome and haven't been able to fix them yet. I'm guessing this will be a big job. Any help is appreciated.
Thanks

messages.author: acb750e476c0ff5d
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts:
I now know that I definitely have markers in duplicate positions. I figured that out from the SNP_Map file from the GigaMUGA data. I've tried drop.dupmarkers, drop.nullmarkers, and jittermap, but still can't get past the singular matrix error. I'm also trying plot.map(pull.map(cross),est.map(cross)) to look at the map. I'm doing each chromosome on its own because of the large number of markers. What should I expect and what should I look for on a map that is messed up? They all look different, but still similar.
Thanks

messages.author: 1ed164e293294b48
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts:
On Thu, Aug 25, 2016 at 11:48:11AM -0700, william...@cchmc.org wrote:
> I'm having a similar error, the "singular matrix" error. I also had the "Some markers at the same position" error. I assume this is the map problem that Danny was talking about. I'm trying to follow his recommendation, but I'm using GigaMUGA data for my analysis. I started with 143,259 SNPs (the whole set) and dwindled it down to 31,642 SNPs that are informative between the two mouse strains of interest. Is this data set too big? I seem to have problem markers on every chromosome and haven't been able to fix them yet. I'm guessing this will be a big job. Any help is appreciated.
> Thanks

If your data is in VCF format you can use my bio-vcf to apply sensible
filters to this data. I have an example of an approach with GTEx here:

https://github.com/pjotrp/bioruby-vcf/blob/master/doc/GTEx_reduce.md

It may also be interesting to use an LMM on your data - in addition to
scanone and MQM. Karl has an implementation in R/qtl2, and we have one
on http://genenetwork.org/ (use Genenetwork 2 to try pylmm).

Pjotr Prins

messages.author: acb750e476c0ff5d
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts:
Unfortunately the data is not in VCF format. I'm using GigaMUGA data that comes as text files, including a Sample_Map file and FinalReport file (the FinalReport file is large at 143,259 SNPs by 96 samples). These files are combined with a GigaMUGA SNPS file that are run through the argyle program for R. From there the data goes into R/qtl. I'm not as familiar with the LMM (Linear Mixed Models) approach. I've already done scanone and am trying to figure out the MQM or scantwo for the data. My collaborators already have a gene of interest and are hoping to find a modifier or something else that works in conjunction with their known and fixed gene of interest. The QTL corresponding to the gene of interest does seem to be popping up on the scanone runs. Now I'm hoping to give them another QTL to investigate for their model.
Thanks for the help.
Bill

messages.author: acb750e476c0ff5d
messages.subject: Re: singular matrix error for mqmscan
parts: I did what John suggested. I removed markers at duplicate positions, which took quite a while with my large marker set. I also reduced my marker set further using the pickMarkerSubset function. I had to play around and see how much I needed to reduce it by. Beyond that we'll have to wait and see if a better fix comes along in the future.
